Chronic renal failure accelerates atherogenesis in apolipoprotein E-deficient mice. Cardiovascular mortality is 10 to 20 times increased in patients with chronic renal failure (CRF). Risk factors for atherosclerosis are abundant in patients with CRF. However, the pathogenesis of cardiovascular disease in CRF remains to be elucidated. The effect of CRF on the development of atherosclerosis in apolipoprotein E-deficient male mice was examined. Seven-week-old mice underwent 5/6 nephrectomy (CRF, n = 28), unilateral nephrectomy (UNX, n = 24), or no surgery (n = 23).
